statement: Nvidia is testing Rubin Ultra configurations at 192GB and 256GB of HBM, down from a planned 1TB, with some samples reverting to prior-generation HBM4
why: Falling back to smaller and older memory stacks is a workaround that keeps GPUs shipping but signals real scarcity of the newest memory.

impact.mechanism: Substituting lower-capacity or previous-generation memory preserves unit output and may lower price, but reduces per-GPU capability for AI server deployments.

evidence.source: Seoul Economic Daily (citing The Information / SemiAnalysis reporting)
evidence.excerpt: the company is now testing configurations at 192GB and 256GB, with some samples reverting to HBM4 (the previous generation) instead of HBM4E

confidence.basis: Secondary press relaying unnamed-source reporting; configurations described as under evaluation, not finalized.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend falling -> falling); sources: Seoul Economic Daily (citing The Information / SemiAnalysis reporting)
